transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-06-21
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ruth Chen (Redwood SE), Jared Lowe (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Atlas CTO), Ethan Brooks (Atlas ML), Rina Kapoor (Atlas PM), Liam O'Neil (Atlas Infra)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood demo of Console tracing, walked through request timeline, error buckets, request log search and export, and a live debugging flow showing KV cache bypass to reproduce a failure. Customer asked about audit logs, SSO, VPC/private deploy options, and cost impacts of increased tracing.

00:00:05 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, I'll kick off, introduce Ruth and Jared who will do the demo. Maya, Ethan, thanks for making time. Does the time still work?
00:00:14 Maya: Yeah this works, thanks. We got Rina and Liam on too.
00:00:20 Ruth: Cool, quick agenda: tracing overview, error analysis, request logs, then a short live debugging flow where we replay a failing request. We'll also cover RBAC and export/retention settings.
00:00:33 Ethan: Quick ask — we've been seeing sporadic timeouts on long context calls; want to see how Redwood surfaces that.
00:00:40 Jared: Yep we'll show the latency heatmaps and the per-route percentiles — that should help.

00:01:15 Ruth: All right, opening the Console — this is the traces page. You'll see a list of recent request traces, each trace represents a top-level API call and includes spans for routing, model inference, KV cache hit/miss, and downstream calls. Note: transcription may show misspellings of product names.
00:01:42 Maya: Can you filter by model version? We pin models so want to separate v1/v2 traffic.
00:01:50 Ruth: Yes filter at the top, model and version are first-class filters. You can also filter by route, region, or by customer tag.
00:02:12 Samir: We also have labels for Dedicated vs Hosted so you can compare latency across deployment modes.

00:03:00 Ruth: Here's an example trace — top shows overall duration 1.2s, breakdown: routing 50ms, batch queue 120ms, model 800ms, postproc 230ms. You can expand spans to see logs.
00:03:30 Ethan: Those batch queue numbers — how do they change under burst? We have spiky traffic.
00:03:38 Ruth: Good question. We show queue length and batching histograms. Autoscaling policies can be tuned and we give recommendations in Optimize. Under burst you will see higher batch sizes and potentially higher tail latency. We can annotate rollouts to compare.

00:05:02 Jared: Now error analysis page — we bucket errors by status (5xx, model-err, timeout, malformed request). You can click a bucket and see representative requests and stack traces. Note: some stack traces in transcripts may be truncated.
00:05:28 Rina: Can we see aggregated root causes? Like whether timeouts correlate with KV cache misses or long generation lengths?
00:05:36 Ruth: Yes, the error analyzer correlates with trace tags. For example, we often see timeouts with high token counts and KV-cache misses; the UI surfaces correlations and allows drilling into request logs.
00:06:10 Ethan: If we want to reproduce a failure locally, can we export the exact request including KV state?
00:06:18 Ruth: We can export the request payload and environment (model version, sequence lengths, feature flags). KV state export is sensitive — we don't export customer KV cache contents for privacy, but we provide a trace-level marker showing whether the request was a cache hit or miss. For reproductions we suggest a replay mode that bypasses KV to simulate a miss or force a cold-start. We'll demo that now.

00:07:25 Ruth: Switching to request logs. You can search by request ID, time range, route, model, or custom tags. Here's a request that failed with 504. Click into the trace to see spans and logs.
00:07:48 Samir: Note the top of the trace includes a link to the raw log export and a permalink you can share with teammates. Permalinks respect RBAC.
00:08:03 Maya: Speaking of RBAC, can we limit who sees traces vs full logs? We need to ensure certain teams can't see PII.
00:08:12 Jared: Yes, we have granular RBAC: view-trace, export-logs, view-raw-payload are separate permissions and map to your SAML groups.
00:08:22 Liam: Do logs include user prompt content by default? We need to redact sensitive fields.
00:08:30 Ruth: By default we store request metadata and hashed prompt signatures; full payload storage is configurable. For regulated use we'll recommend disabling full payload retention and enabling structured redaction rules. We'll send the redaction docs.

00:09:10 Ruth: Demo time — I'll trigger a replay of this failing request with KV-cache forced bypass. You can see on the left a toggle "Replay with cache bypass".
00:09:22 Ethan: Nice. That should show whether the failure is caching related or model path related.
00:09:31 Ruth: Starting replay... replay completed, response returned, and latency dropped by ~300ms but error disappeared. In the trace you can see a spike in batch queue time on the original request correlated with a large batch size.
00:10:05 Maya: So likely a batching edge-case? Maybe requests with long contexts are delaying the batch.
00:10:12 Ruth: Exactly, we often recommend soft limits on max tokens per request or prioritization rules. Also Optimize can suggest quantization and batching tweaks.

00:11:00 Ethan: About tracing retention — how long do traces stay? We need 90 days for audits.
00:11:07 Samir: Hosted plan defaults to 30 days; enterprise can configure retention up to 1 year and longer with archive exports to your S3. Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable in your deployment.
00:11:22 Rina: Do archived traces still include request payloads?
00:11:28 Ruth: Archived exports can include full payloads if you opt-in, otherwise they're metadata-only.

00:12:15 Jared: Next, alerting — you can create alerts on error rate, p50/p95 latency, or new error signatures. Alerts can create Jira tickets or Slack messages with trace links.
00:12:36 Maya: Can alerts be scoped per-team? We don't want infra alerts spamming product.
00:12:42 Ruth: Yep, alerting has scopes and routing rules.

00:14:00 Samir: quick pause — any legal/security red flags so far?
00:14:06 Maya: SOC2 is critical, also we need to understand KMS integration and whether keys are customer-managed for private deployment.
00:14:15 Samir: For Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and we log KMS operations; we'll send network diagram and SOC2 certs.

00:15:30 Ruth: Back to the Console — request log export. You can bulk-export to CSV/JSON or stream to your S3. We also support direct forward to their SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). Exports include trace ID, timestamps, latency breakdowns, and optional payload hashes.
00:15:56 Liam: How does the stream perform at high volume? We run millions of calls daily.
00:16:05 Jared: We support high-throughput streaming exports; for very high volume customers we recommend Dedicated with direct egress to your VPC. We'll size the export pipeline with you.

00:17:30 Ruth: Now a short walkthrough of the error analyzer's clustering UI. We cluster by fingerprinted stack and model error signature. You can accept a cluster and mark it as resolved or assign to a team.
00:17:50 Rina: Can we annotate clusters with internal notes?
00:17:55 Ruth: Yes, notes, tags, and you can pin related traces. Those annotations are visible only to your org.

00:19:20 Ethan: For debugging, how granular are spans? Do we see token-level timings?
00:19:28 Ruth: We record model-level spans and, optionally, token-level generation timings if you enable verbose tracing — note that adds overhead and cost, so usually used for short-term investigations.
00:19:45 Maya: Is verbose tracing available on Dedicated or just Hosted?
00:19:52 Ruth: It's available across modes but on Dedicated you can choose to run it selectively on specific pools to minimize cost.

00:21:05 Samir: Talk briefly about canary rollouts — Console can compare two model versions side-by-side in the traces view and surface regression alerts based on custom eval sets and live metrics.
00:21:22 Rina: We want automatic rollback if error rate jumps.
00:21:27 Jared: You can set an auto-fallback policy: if p99 or error rate exceeds threshold, traffic shifts to the previous stable variant.

00:22:40 Ruth: Quick note about cost — extensive tracing and payload retention increases unit costs. Optimize will give recommendations on sampling rate and what spans to keep. We generally suggest sampling verbose traces at 1-5% for production.

00:24:00 Maya: For PII-sensitive calls we might need to never log payloads. Can we set route-level overrides?
00:24:08 Ruth: Yes, route-level retention overrides exist. You can also redact fields via regex rules.

00:25:10 Ethan: About request replay — if we replay a request at peak, will that count against our production quotas?
00:25:18 Samir: Replays count as requests against your quota by default; we can provide a replay sandbox or a separate replay allowance for POC. 
00:25:30 Rina: Good. Also we need a way to correlate our internal request IDs with Redwood trace IDs.
00:25:37 Ruth: Trace IDs are part of the headers; we automatically index cust_request_id if you send it. We'll show an example.

00:27:00 Ruth: I'll attach the trace permalink into chat now (link placeholder).
00:27:05 Samir: We'll also share a short video clip and the benchmark spreadsheet that shows tail latency across models.

00:28:20 Ethan: One more infra question — for Private/on-prem what logs do we still need to provide?
00:28:28 Samir: Private runs in your network, so you control persistence. Our control plane can be private too; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM without leaving the VPC.

00:30:05 Maya: Ok, roadmap fit — we're hoping for a July pilot. Our success criteria: reproducible debugging within 48 hours, <200ms median inference improvement on the failing route, and clear audit logs for SOC2.
00:30:22 Samir: That seems reasonable. Proposed next steps: Samir to send pilot agreement and pricing; Ruth to run repro; Ethan to send failing request IDs; schedule POC kickoff.

00:31:10 Rina: Minor nit — the UI search sometimes returns similar IDs, fuzzy match?
00:31:16 Ruth: We have exact and fuzzy modes, plus column filters. We'll include a short cheat sheet.

00:33:00 Jared: Demo wrap-up. Any final questions?
00:33:05 Liam: SSO — we use Okta. How long to get SAML integration?
00:33:12 Samir: Usually 2-3 business days to configure SAML SSO and map groups; we'll have templates for Okta.
00:33:25 Maya: Also need data residency in EU for some subsets of data.
00:33:31 Samir: We have EU regions and customer-controlled retention; for EU-only residency we'd recommend Dedicated/Private.

00:34:00 Ruth: Quick show of an exported CSV sample — columns include trace_id, timestamp, route, model, p50/p95, error_code, payload_hash.
00:34:20 Ethan: Looks good. We'll try the replay with our sample dataset.

00:35:05 Samir: Recap of action items and owners verbally: I'll send SOC2 and pricing; Ruth will run a repro and share notes; Ethan will send request IDs; Jared will include export config doc.
00:35:25 Maya: Thanks, this was helpful.
00:35:30 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links and scheduling.

Transcript notes: occasional ASR mistakes present (e.g., KV-cache spelled as K-V cache or "kay-vee cache", product names slightly mutated). There were short cross-talks around 00:09 and 00:33.

End of transcript.
